title: Capacity and Growth
goal: Understand preallocation and heap reallocation in String.

sections.text: You know dynamic array buffers in Go or Java allocate extra space to avoid copying memory on every append. `String` in Rust works the same way.

sections.code:
let mut s = String::with_capacity(10);
println!("{}", s.capacity());
sections.caption: with_capacity reserves byte storage upfront.

sections.text: Calling `String::new()` creates a string with zero capacity. Appending text with `push_str` reallocates heap memory whenever length exceeds capacity.

sections.caption: Pushing within capacity avoids extra allocations.

sections.text: Length is the number of bytes stored right now. Capacity is the total number of bytes reserved before a new allocation takes place.

explanation: Understand preallocation and heap reallocation in String.
